page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; running head at the top centre; page number 9 at the top right. No margin notes, no footnotes, no catchword.

p.i: culcant isti, quos obscurissimos extra propriam urbem, imò in urbe sua vix cognitos, nulla vestrum pro legitimis velit sine pudore admittere. Tu verò antiquissima & purissima Divæ Antistes & Cancellarie Laurenti Doctissime, & Excellentissime apud Regem nostrum, Matris communis causam age, & ut teneris, Defensor animosus, propugnator strenuus, & Patronus vigilans adveni. Hoc abs te illa poscit, hoc poscimus omnes, quod nec eius precibus, nec ei, quam in tam Augusta sustines Academia, dignitati possis denegare, &c.

main_text.p: Voicy les termes de la Censure de l'Escho-le de Medecine de Paris contre ce Mayerne Turquet. Collegium Medicorum in Academia Parisiensi legitimè congregatum, audita renun-ciatione censorum, quibus demandata erat provin-cia examinandi Apologiam sub nomine Mayerni Turqueti editam, ipsam unanimi consensu damnat, tanquam famosum libellum, mendacibus convitiis, & impudentibus calumniis refertum, quæ non nisi ab homine imperito, impudente, temulento & furio-so proficisci potuerunt: Ipsum Turquetum indignum iudicat, qui usquam Medicinam faciat, propter te-meritatem, impudentiam, & veram Medicinæ igno-rationem: Omnes verò Medicos, qui ubique gentium & locorum Medicinam exercent, hortatur, ut ipsum Turquetum, similiáque hominum & opinionum por-tenta, à se suisque finibus arceant; & in Hippocra-

page.notes: The first paragraph appears wholly in italic; the names Laurenti and Regem nostrum may be roman in the original, which I could not separate with certainty. The long s has been written as plain s throughout, including in the running head ("Efcholes" as "Escholes"). Printed hyphens at line ends are kept. The printed text is unbroken at the page foot, so the final word "Hippocra-" stays a fragment for the next page.
